metrics.loss_month_names: concentrated in Jan, Feb, Mar, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec across years

findings.brand: Aventon is the largest e-bike brand (41% of bike sales), followed by Velotric and NCM. Brands treated as exclusive-dealer lines in this scenario (Aventon, Stromer, Velotric, Bulls) generate 70% of bike revenue in the demonstration data. Margin varies from 25.4% to 32.5% by brand, so mix shifts matter as much as volume.
findings.models: 36 of 56 e-bike models generate 80% of bike revenue. Best seller: Aventon Level 3 ($298,576, 127 units). The bottom 10 models together contribute 6.7% of bike revenue yet tie up floor space and capital.
findings.category: E-bike categories carry 27-31% gross margin, while accessories and parts earn 47-49%. Accessories are only 7% of retail revenue but are a high-margin attachment to every bike sale.
findings.atv: Average transaction value is $2,764 when an e-bike is included versus $158 for accessory/parts-only baskets. Only 65% of bike transactions include an accessory (1.07 accessory lines per bike sale), which is the clearest low-cost revenue lever.
findings.growth: Retail net sales were $2.39M in 2024 and $2.33M in 2025 (-2.6%). January-September 2026 is +8.7% versus the same period of 2025 (bike units +5.9%). Demand is strongly seasonal: April-August generates 69% of 2025 retail revenue.
findings.discount: Discounts on e-bikes total $149,746 over the period; $78,805 of that is discretionary (not tied to a promotion). Margin falls from 29.5% at list price to 21.2% at the deepest band - each 5 points of discount removes roughly a fifth of bike gross profit.
findings.pnl: Trailing-twelve-month (Oct 2025-Sep 2026) revenue is $3.15M with operating profit of $38,617. The store loses money in 17 of 33 months (concentrated in Jan, Feb, Mar, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec across years) because fixed costs (~$80,253/month) exceed winter contribution. Break-even revenue is about $252,623/month ($3.03M/year) at a 31.8% contribution margin; the margin of safety is 4%.
findings.inventory: E-bike inventory turns 4.1x per year (~89 days on hand) and accessories 15.5x. 39 products (A class) drive 80% of consumption value. 8 products hold more than six months of cover, tying up $98,123 at cost.
findings.stockouts: Stockouts cost an estimated $421,527 of revenue ($128,835 gross profit) in the last 12 months, including 153 e-bikes. Roughly 14% of e-bike demand went unmet. Losses concentrate in April-June, when the flat, non-seasonal reorder policy cannot keep pace with demand - while the same policy leaves excess stock in the autumn.
findings.leads: 11,443 leads converted at 19.4% overall. Leads who took a test ride converted at 39% versus 7% without - an association, not proof of causation, but strong support for pushing test-ride bookings. Among paid channels, Email/Newsletter has the lowest cost per conversion ($104) and Social Media the highest ($200).
findings.clv: 25% of active customers have two or more purchase/service interactions. 77% of 2024 e-bike buyers returned in 2025 (mostly for service). Estimated 5-year customer lifetime value for an e-bike buyer is $1,161 in gross profit ($772 at the first sale plus discounted service/accessory follow-on), which caps sensible acquisition cost.
findings.service: Service generated $651,667 over the last 12 months at a 61% gross margin - the highest-margin revenue stream. Average turnaround rises from 4.5 days off-season to 10.8 days in June-July, and satisfaction falls from 4.51 to 3.64. Peak utilisation reaches 123% of technician capacity because new-bike assembly competes with repairs. Warranty work (263 orders) nets $27,095 after technician time.
findings.promotions: Spring Kick-off Event shows the strongest estimated incremental gross profit; End-of-Season Clearance the weakest (-$27,956 across events). Deep, broad discounts lift units but can reduce gross profit. A controlled test (e.g. alternating brands or weeks) is needed before drawing causal conclusions.
findings.weather: Holding month, weekday and year constant, each additional 1 deg C of daily temperature is associated with +2.3% bike sales (95% CI +1.4% to +3.3%), and each mm of rain with -1.1%. Weather is real ECCC data; the sales response is built into the synthetic data, so a pilot should re-estimate it on Prairie Pulse E-Bikes' actual sales.
